rules.title: Reglas de Mitchi
rules.intro: [ES] Everything you need to play, from setup to the end of the game.

overview.heading: Resumen
overview.summary: [ES] Mitchi is a dice game for two or more players, played over a series of rounds. Each round, you roll to avoid being left with the worst hand. The player with the worst hand takes the points in the pot. When the game ends, the player with the fewest points wins.

youNeed.heading: Qué necesitas
youNeed.paper: [ES] A pen and paper to keep score

setup.heading: Preparación
setup.pointLimit: [ES] Agree a point limit. 25 is usual. Choose a lower limit for a shorter game.
setup.whoStarts: [ES] Decide who starts. Everyone rolls one die, and the highest roll starts. If the highest roll is tied, those players roll again. Play goes clockwise.

hands.heading: Manos
hands.intro: [ES] A hand is the two dice you finish your turn with. There are six groups of hands, from best to worst:
hands.allHandsLink: Las 21 manos están incluidas en la <reference>referencia rápida</reference>.

rollLimit.heading: [ES] The starting player sets the roll limit
rollLimit.rolls: [ES] The starting player rolls both dice, up to three times, and can stop after any roll. After each roll, they can:
rollLimit.keepOne: [ES] keep one die and re-roll the other
rollLimit.newChoice: [ES] Each roll is a new choice. Keeping a die on one roll does not mean keeping it on the next. Re-rolling one die still counts as a roll.
rollLimit.setsLimit: [ES] The number of rolls the starting player uses is the <term>roll limit</term> for everyone else that round.
rollLimit.example: [ES] The starting player rolls six-three in two rolls. Everyone else gets up to two rolls.

everyoneElse.heading: [ES] Everyone else
everyoneElse.turn: [ES] Everyone else takes a turn in clockwise order, with the same choices, up to the roll limit. You do not have to use every roll. Stop when you are happy with your hand.
everyoneElse.worstHandSoFar: [ES] You never need the best hand. You only need to beat the <term>worst hand so far</term>: the lowest-ranked hand rolled this round. It changes as players finish their turn, so a later player may have less to beat than an earlier one.
everyoneElse.example1: [ES] Player {a} rolls six-four in one. Player {b} rolls five-one. Player {c} now needs five-two or better, because five-one is the worst hand so far.
everyoneElse.example2: [ES] Player {a} rolls five-four in three. Player {b} rolls six-two in one. That already beats five-four, so Player {b} stops.

scoring.heading: La puntuación de la ronda
scoring.startingPot: [ES] Every round starts with 1 point in <term>the pot</term>.
scoring.mitchis: [ES] The first Mitchi rolled replaces that point with 2 points. Each Mitchi after that adds 2 more, so the pot is 2 points for every Mitchi rolled.
scoring.takeThePot: [ES] At the end of the round, the player with the worst hand <term>takes the pot</term> and adds the points to their score. They start the next round.

tieBreaks.heading: Desempates
tieBreaks.intro: [ES] If two or more players are tied on the worst hand, they play a <term>tie-break</term> to decide who takes the pot.
tieBreaks.rollOnce: [ES] Roll once each. Only the tied players roll, with no re-rolls. Go in the opposite direction to the last round or tie-break, starting with the last player to roll.
tieBreaks.addMitchis: [ES] Add 2 points for each Mitchi rolled in the tie-break.
tieBreaks.worstHandTakes: [ES] The worst hand takes the pot. If players tie again, go back to step 1 with only those players.

example.tied: [ES] Three players tie on the worst hand
example.takesPot: [ES] One player has the worst hand and takes the pot

winning.heading: Ganar la partida
winning.gameEnds: [ES] The game ends when any player reaches the point limit. The player with the fewest points wins.
winning.tiedOnFewest: [ES] If players are tied on the fewest points, they roll once each, and the best hand wins.

reference.title: Referencia rápida
reference.standfirst: Todo lo que necesitas durante la partida, en una sola pantalla.

ranking.heading: Clasificación de las manos
ranking.caption: Las manos de Mitchi, clasificadas de mejor a peor

scoring.heading: Puntuación
scoring.note: Los puntos de Mitchi cuentan los saque quien los saque. La peor mano se lleva el bote y empieza la siguiente ronda.
scoring.rule2: Una tirada cada uno, no hasta tres.
scoring.rule3: El bote se dobla antes de tirar.
scoring.rule4: El orden se invierte, empezando por el último jugador que tiró.
scoring.rule5: Cada Mitchi que se saque añade 2 puntos más al bote.
scoring.rule6: ¿Sigue el empate? Se repite. El bote se dobla otra vez y el orden se invierte otra vez.
scoring.limit: La partida termina en cuanto un jugador alcanza el límite de puntos, normalmente 25. Gana quien menos puntos tenga. Si varios jugadores empatan con la puntuación más baja, cada uno saca una mano y gana la mejor.

speak.title: Mitchi Speak
speak.standfirst: Los nombres que se usan en la mesa en lugar de los oficiales. Nada de esto cambia cómo se juega: una mano llamada por su nombre en Mitchi Speak se juega exactamente igual que con su nombre oficial.
speak.caption: Las manos y sus nombres en Mitchi Speak
speak.footnote: La mayoría de los nombres se han olvidado. Esta lista es lo que se ha recuperado hasta ahora.

terminology.title: Terminología
terminology.standfirst: Todos los términos en los que se apoyan las reglas, definidos una sola vez. Y luego, los nombres que se usan de verdad en la mesa.

about.title: Acerca de Mitchi
about.standfirst: De dónde viene el juego y cómo se reconstruyeron estas reglas.
about.origin: Mitchi se aprendió viajando por España, aunque no de un jugador español. De dónde venía antes no se sabe, y esta web no lo presenta como un juego tradicional español.
about.reconstruction: Estas reglas son una reconstrucción. Algunas se recordaban, otras se recuperaron preguntando a quienes jugaban. Donde ha habido que fijar una regla en lugar de recordarla, se ha fijado tal y como se jugaba en realidad.
about.speak: También hay un vocabulario propio. Las manos tienen apodos que no significan nada para quien no estuviera en la mesa. No forman parte del juego, pero <speak>están escritos igualmente</speak>.

handGroups.withinGroup: [ES] Within a group, the higher hand wins: double-six beats double-five, and six-five beats six-four. The worst hand in the game is three-one.

mitchi.name: Mitchi
mitchi.definition: El juego, y también su mejor mano: un 2 y un 1.

hand.name: Mano
hand.definition: Los dos dados con los que terminas tu turno.

roll.name: Tirada
roll.definition: Cada vez que se tiran uno o los dos dados. Volver a tirar un solo dado sigue contando como una tirada.

rolledIn.name: [ES] In one, in two, in three
rolledIn.definition: [ES] How many rolls a hand took: six-three in two.

round.name: [ES] Round
round.definition: [ES] Every player takes one turn, then the worst hand takes the pot.

turn.name: [ES] Turn
turn.definition: [ES] Your rolls in a round, up to the roll limit.

startingPlayer.name: [ES] Starting player
startingPlayer.definition: [ES] The player who rolls first in a round and sets the roll limit.

rollLimit.name: Límite de tiradas
rollLimit.definition: El número de tiradas que tiene cada jugador en una ronda, fijado por el jugador inicial.

doubles.name: [ES] Doubles
doubles.definition: [ES] Both dice showing the same number.

worstHandSoFar.name: Peor mano hasta ahora
worstHandSoFar.definition: [ES] The lowest-ranked hand rolled so far in a round. The hand you need to beat.

pot.name: El bote
pot.definition: [ES] The points at stake in a round. It starts at 1.

takeThePot.name: Llevarse el bote
takeThePot.definition: Sumar a tu puntuación todos los puntos del bote.

tieBreak.name: Desempate
tieBreak.definition: Una tirada entre los jugadores que empatan en la peor mano.

points.name: Puntos
points.definition: [ES] Your score. Points are bad: the fewest wins.

pointLimit.name: Límite de puntos
pointLimit.definition: La puntuación que termina la partida en cuanto un jugador la alcanza. Normalmente 25.
